notes: Inbound SMB lead (self-serve signup) complaining about intermittent latency spikes when users hit chat support bot. Minimal infra knowledge, running in public cloud. Key quotes: 'sometimes responses take 6-8s which breaks UX' and 'we saw regional differences — west coast users slower than east'. Looking for quick tuning before committing to paid tier. Primary requests: lower p95 latency, guidance on region choice, recommended timeout settings, prompt length best practices, and cost tradeoffs for batching. Initial rep guidance provided: prefer region nearest users (us-east-1) for east/central NA users; test eu-west-1 for EU customers. Recommend connection timeout 5-10s, request timeout 60s for full generation; use streaming API to improve perceived latency. Prompt guidance: truncate long system messages, keep user + system context <= 1024 tokens where possible, cap max_tokens to 256 for chat responses to reduce tail latency. Suggested perf checklist shared (see Drive link). Also advised temporary mitigations: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, reduce model size for lower-latency paths (try small/medium open model), and tune batching (small batch sizes, concurrency=2 for low latency). Customer is cost-sensitive — asked for rough estimate of token vs latency tradeoffs. Procurement wants SOC2 doc before moving to evaluation. POC plan: 2-week POC on hosted_api, run region A/B (us-east vs us-west), enable streaming + shorter max_tokens, collect token-level latency traces from Console. Owen (SE) to join next call to review logs.
